topic: Changes in Materials When Heated, Cooled, or Mixed
key_concepts: Heating increases the temperature of a material.
Cooling decreases the temperature of a material.
Heating can change a material's size, shape, form, and texture.
Heating can change solids to liquids through melting.
Cooling can change liquids back to solids.
Butter, chocolate, crayons, and candle wax melt when heated.
Melted materials such as crayon, chocolate, and butter harden when cooled.
Water and soft drinks become solid when placed in a freezer.
Hot water dissolves solids such as sugar and coffee faster than cold water.
Solid materials can be mixed with other solid materials.
Some solid-solid mixtures show one phase or two phases.
Solid materials can also be mixed with liquid materials.
